name: How a URL shortener works
description: The classic system-design interview favorite — clients, API, cache, database and analytics — explained step by step with narration.

narration.1: This is the system behind every short link you have ever clicked. It starts, as always, with the browser.
narration.2: A load balancer is the front door. It spreads millions of requests across many identical servers so no single machine drowns.
narration.3: The shorten API takes a long URL and mints a short code — usually six characters of letters and digits, which gives fifty-six billion combinations.
narration.4: The redirect service does the opposite job: given a short code, find the long URL and answer with a redirect — in under ten milliseconds.
narration.5: Redis keeps the most popular links in memory. Ninety percent of clicks hit a tiny fraction of links, so the cache absorbs almost everything.
narration.6: The database is the source of truth. Every code and its destination lives here, replicated so nothing is ever lost.
narration.7: Every click also drops an event onto a queue. The redirect never waits for analytics — that is the secret to staying fast.
narration.8: A worker drains the queue into the warehouse, where dashboards count clicks by country, device and hour. And that is the whole system.
